blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Lean verifies that a formal proof establishes its stated proposition under declared assumptions, but does not check whether that proposition faithfully expresses the mathematical claim in a manuscript. Assessing this correspondence requires interpreting the main theorem through its project dependencies, which may be scattered throughout a large development. We introduce MechAlign, a framework for project-level semantic alignment review that combines formal dependency extraction with LLM-based assessment. Its extraction tool, LeanTrace, constructs a statement dependency graph from elaborated declarations, retaining definition bodies and structure constraints while excluding proof bodies and stopping at an explicit library boundary. The reviewer uses this context to investigate alignment and report discrepancies with localized evidence. We conduct a preliminary review of 201 main results from 173 OpenAI Math projects, using supplied informal descriptions and available paper context. A hyperbolic-group case illustrates how dependency inspection localizes a missing dimensional constraint relative to the manuscript, consistent with the upstream declaration of formalization scope. We also construct LeanReviewBench, comprising 501 fixed claim-statement-context triples from OpenAI Math, Fermat's Last Theorem, and Kakeya, with description provenance recorded. The resource supports controlled comparisons of more project-level semantic alignment evaluations.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Recent advances in large language models have enabled the generation of mathematical proofs at increasing scale [ Cao et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026a ; Zhang et al., 2026a ; OpenAI, 2026b ] .
Lean formalization is also used to verify the stated results. For example, OpenAI’s mathematical research collection includes Lean projects for 173 manuscripts [ OpenAI, 2026b ] .
Lean checks that a formal proof establishes its stated proposition under the declared assumptions [ de Moura and Ullrich, 2021 ] , but it does not check whether that proposition faithfully expresses the mathematical claim in the manuscript.
This leaves a semantic gap: Does the statement proved in the Lean project faithfully express the mathematical claim made in the manuscript? Answering this question requires establishing the mathematical meaning of the formal statement.
In a Lean project, that meaning is determined not only by the main theorem declaration but also by the definitions and constraints it refers to.

近期在大语言模型上的进步,使得数学证明的生成规模越来越大[曹等,2026;刘等,2026a;张等,2026a;OpenAI,2026b].
精益正规化也用于验证所声明的结果. 例如,OpenAI的数学研究收藏包括了为173个手稿所设计的Lean项目[OpenAI, 2026b].

这留下了语义上的差距: 该声明在"利恩"项目中被证明是否忠实地表达了手稿中的数学要求? 回答这个问题需要确定正式声明的数学含义.
在利恩项目中,这一含义不仅由主要定理声明所决定,而且还由它所提到的定义和制约所决定.

blocks.en:
For example, a theorem stated using a predicate defined within the project may appear to match the manuscript, even though the predicate encodes additional assumptions or a weaker conclusion.
Interpreting the predicate may, in turn, require tracing its dependencies.
We use project-level alignment review to mean assessing a selected formal result against its informal claim by examining the project declarations that determine the result’s meaning.

我们利用项目一级的调整审查,即通过审查决定结果含义的项目申报,对照非正式索赔评估选定的正式结果。

blocks.en:
Several methods can be used for project-level alignment review.
A statement-only reviewer sees the main Lean declaration, but cannot inspect these supporting declarations.
Providing full project access makes them available, but leaves the reviewer to locate and connect the relevant evidence.
We therefore ask how to organize these declarations to support both evidence gathering and mathematical assessment.

提供完整的项目访问机会可以提供,但让审查者查找和连接有关证据。
因此,我们询问如何组织这些声明以支持证据收集和数学评估。

blocks.en:
We introduce MechAlign , a framework for project-level semantic alignment review. Its formal evidence extractor, LeanTrace , starts from a selected theorem’s elaborated type and follows references through declaration types and non-proof definition bodies.
It retains structural constraints and stops expansion at an explicit library boundary, producing a statement dependency graph that organizes formal evidence around the selected result.
MechAlign’s LLM-based reviewer inspects declarations and follows graph edges to assess alignment between the informal claim and the formal result, reporting discrepancies with supporting evidence.
The extracted context supports this assessment but may not suffice to resolve every question of mathematical interpretation.
Refer to Figure 1 for the structure of MechAlign.

blocks.en:
Our primary application is OpenAI Math [ OpenAI, 2026b ] , where we inspect 201 selected main results from 173 projects and identify candidate discrepancies for further review.
The HyperbolicObstruction case illustrates how inspecting a statement and its supporting structure reveals that the manuscript’s two-dimensionality requirement is not explicitly retained, consistent with the upstream declaration of formalization scope.
We extend the extracted contexts with 200 selected targets from Fermat’s Last Theorem [ Anthropic, 2026 ] and 100 from Kakeya [ Project Numina, 2026b ] to construct LeanReviewBench , a resource of 501 fixed instances.
Each instance pairs a supplied informal claim with a selected formal statement and includes the statement’s extracted dependency context.
This structure supports a controlled, reproducible comparison of statement-only, full-project, and dependency-guided review in terms of discrepancy detection, evidence localization, and review cost.
Supplementary collections broaden coverage of mathematical topics and dependency structures.
Because their descriptions are derived from Lean, they support consistency checks against the supplied text but do not independently establish fidelity to a manuscript.
The comparative evaluation and human adjudication remain to be completed.

blocks.en: Our contributions are threefold: • We formulate a project-level semantic alignment review in which a selected formal result is assessed against its informal claim through the declarations that determine its meaning. • We introduce MechAlign, combining LeanTrace’s extraction of statement dependencies with an LLM-based reviewer that inspects the resulting graph and reports localized semantic discrepancies. • We construct LeanReviewBench, comprising 501 review instances from OpenAI Math, Fermat’s Last Theorem, and Kakeya, and we define a controlled comparison of statement-only, full-project, and dependency-guided review.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Autoformalization converts informal problems into formal statements that can be verified in Lean 4 [ de Moura and Ullrich, 2021 ] .
Herald [ Gao et al., 2025 ] annotates Mathlib 4 with natural language and trains a dedicated Lean 4 translator.
Process-driven Autoformalization [ Lu et al., 2024 ] incorporates Lean compiler feedback through process-supervised verification.
SAIR-Comb [ Jiang et al., 2026 ] combines structure-aware refinement with expert iteration and reinforcement learning for autoformalization in combinatorics.
Agent-based approaches further integrate generation, checking, and refinement into interactive workflows.
MASA [ Zhang et al., 2025 ] coordinates agents for formalization, syntactic checking, semantic assessment, and iterative repair.
LeanMarathon [ Zhang et al., 2026b ] uses an evolving blueprint to coordinate agents across research-level formalization tasks.
Numina-Lean-Agent [ Liu et al., 2026b ] combines a general-purpose coding agent with Lean interaction and theorem retrieval tools through MCP.
MechMath [ Qiu et al., 2026 ] uses sorrifier-driven decomposition to isolate unresolved subgoals while preserving the surrounding verified proof structure.
Numina Fuse [ Project Numina, 2026a ] provides a desktop workspace for developing Lean formalizations with AI agents. These advances increase the need to review completed formalizations.

blocks.en:
Recent work further examines diagnostic detail and contextual dependencies.
FormalRx [ Wang et al., 2026 ] evaluates alignment judgments together with error categorization, localization, and correction. FaithAlign [ Feng et al., 2026 ] introduces phrase-level correspondence annotations with explicit informal context and formal dependencies, while FaithAlign-Gap tests whether evaluators recognize insufficient context.
These efforts motivate studying evidence acquisition as part of alignment review.
LeanTrace supplies an explicit extraction policy for the statement dependencies of a selected result, and the review agent inspects that graph for semantic discrepancies.
Our full-project comparison is intended to test the value of this organization of evidence; the method does not presume that source retrieval or existing alignment systems necessarily fail.

blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: In this section, we first define the project-level semantic alignment task. We then present LeanTrace, a tool for extracting the dependency graph of a selected theorem in a Lean project. Finally, we introduce MechAlign, an agent that uses this graph to evaluate semantic alignment in project-level mathematical formalization.

3.2 LeanTrace
blocks.zh: 3.2 利安追踪

blocks.en:
LeanTrace constructs a statement dependency graph from an elaborated Lean project.
Starting from F t F_{t} , the elaborated type of the selected theorem declaration, LeanTrace iteratively collects dependencies through declaration types and non-proof definition bodies.
Newly discovered declarations are processed in turn until no unvisited declarations remain, with library declarations retained as boundary nodes without further expansion.
Theorems and other proof-valued declarations contribute their types, but their proof bodies are neither exposed nor traversed.
blocks.zh:
LeanTrace从精心设计的Lean项目中构建一个语句依赖图.
从 Ft F_{t} 开始, 所选定理声明的详尽类型, LeanTrace 迭代地通过声明类型和不可防定义机构来收集依赖性.
新发现的申报依次进行处理,直到不再保留未经查看的申报,图书馆申报保留为分界节点而不作进一步扩大.
定理和其他有证明价值的申报贡献出其类型,但其证明体既不被暴露,也不被穿行.

blocks.en:
For inductive types, structures, and classes, LeanTrace also follows their constructors and traverses the constructor types, collecting dependencies introduced by field types and constraints even when no field projection appears explicitly in the target statement.
Operating on elaborated declarations captures both explicit dependencies and those introduced by elaboration, including instances, field projections, and generated auxiliary declarations.
blocks.zh:

就详细拟定的申报开展工作,既包括明确的依赖性,也包括详细拟定的依赖性,包括实例、实地预测和产生的辅助申报。

blocks.en:
Recursively expanding Mathlib would introduce a large collection of foundational declarations with complex dependencies.
As a practical choice to keep the extracted context manageable, LeanTrace stops at the library boundary, retaining the names and types of referenced declarations from Mathlib and Lean’s core libraries without traversing their dependencies or expanding their implementations.
The dependency closure 𝒞 \mathcal{C} defined above is understood relative to these extraction rules and this boundary.

作为控制所提取的上下文的一种实际选择,LeanTraces停在了图书馆的边界上,保留了Mathlib和Lean核心图书馆的引用声明的名称和类型,而不穿越它们的依赖性或扩大其执行范围。

blocks.en:
MechAlign is an LLM-assisted framework comprising a Selector , the LeanTrace extraction tool, and a Reviewer .
The Selector uses supplied mappings between informal claims and Lean declarations when available. Otherwise, it searches the manuscript text and Lean source files within a configured scope to identify the manuscript’s main results and select corresponding declarations, supporting each selection with quotations from both sources.
For each target, it records the supplied informal claim I t I_{t} , the selected formal statement F t F_{t} , and the claim’s source.
Claims drawn from Lean comments or documentation are not treated as independently verified manuscript statements.
LeanTrace extracts the dependency context 𝒞 \mathcal{C} for the selected formal statement, retaining declaration types, non-proof values, and dependency relations.

对于每个目标,它记录了所提供的非正式索赔(It I_{t})、选定的正式陈述(Ft F_{t})以及索赔的来源。
从Lean评论或文件中提取的索赔不作为独立核实的手稿说明处理。
LeanTrace为所选的正式语句提取了依赖上下文 C\ mathcal{C},保留了声明类型,非防值,以及依赖关系.

blocks.en: The Reviewer returns an aligned , misaligned , or undetermined judgment, together with explanations for the six dimensions and supporting quotations. Substantive judgments must cite both the supplied informal claim or context and formal evidence. A deterministic evidence check verifies that the quotations occur in the supplied sources; it does not independently validate the informal specification. Ambiguous correspondence or insufficient evidence leads to an undetermined judgment. MechAlign retains selection, extraction, and review records for inspection. The judgments remain model-assisted assessments of the supplied claim rather than formal guarantees of semantic equivalence or manuscript fidelity.

blocks.en: 4 Semantic Alignment of OpenAI Math
blocks.zh: 4 OpenAI 数学语义对齐

blocks.en:
We examine how LeanTrace supports review of a project presented as a proof of a mathematical claim. OpenAI Math provides the primary application.
The study asks whether organizing formal evidence around the selected result helps identify semantic discrepancies and reduces the cost of locating that evidence.
We introduce the review conditions, illustrate dependency inspection through one case, and describe how effectiveness, cost, and limitations are to be compared. Controlled comparative results remain to be completed.

我们审查LeanTrace如何支持审查一个作为数学索赔证据的项目。 OpenAI Math提供了主应用.
研究询问,围绕选定结果组织正式证据是否有助于确定语义差异并降低查找证据的成本。
我们提出审查条件,说明通过一个案例进行的依赖性检查,并说明如何比较效力、费用和限制。 控制下的比较结果仍有待完成。

blocks.en: 4.1 Review Setting and Compared Strategies
blocks.zh: 4.1 审查设置和比较战略

blocks.en:
We used LeanTrace to inspect 201 theorems across 173 projects in openai/math , looking for discrepancies between the stated mathematical claims and their formal encodings.
For each theorem, we compared its informal description in the existing Lean comments with the formal statement and used the extracted dependency graph to inspect the definitions and constraints that determine its meaning.
Upstream docstrings, adjacent comments, and retained paper excerpts provided additional context; generated structural descriptions helped navigate the formal declarations.
This preliminary review assesses correspondence with the supplied descriptions, which have not been independently validated against the manuscripts. Retained paper excerpts provide supplementary context; findings about manuscript fidelity remain candidates pending verification against the original mathematical sources.
The source revision used for the review is listed in Appendix A .

blocks.en:
To evaluate the benefit of dependency-guided review, we design a comparison of three ways of obtaining evidence for the same claim. Statement-only review exposes the main declaration without dependency content. Full-project review permits ordinary source searches and file readings, leaving the reviewer to locate relevant declarations. LeanTrace-assisted review supplies the extracted dependency graph and retained declarations.
The planned comparison holds the model, claim, root, and source revision fixed, with access rules and budgets disclosed.
Each strategy assesses whether the selected formal result expresses the supplied informal claim and reports any discrepancies with its supporting declarations and mathematical explanations.

计划中的比较将模型、索赔、根和源修订固定下来,并公布准入规则和预算。
每项战略都评估选定的正式结果是否表示所提供的非正式索赔,并报告与佐证声明和数学解释有任何出入。

blocks.en: 5 LeanReviewBench: A Reusable Review Resource
blocks.zh: 5 精益审查 座椅:可重复使用的审查资源

blocks.en:
The OpenAI Math study illustrates how reviewing a main result requires interpreting the definitions and constraints behind its formal statement.
To make such reviews repeatable across systems, we construct LeanReviewBench , a reusable collection of the review instances defined in Section 3.1 .
Each instance is a fixed triple x = ( I t , F t , 𝒞 ) x=(I_{t},F_{t},\mathcal{C}) : a supplied informal claim, its selected formal statement, and the dependency context extracted by LeanTrace.
The Selector and LeanTrace stages of MechAlign are completed during benchmark construction.
Evaluation begins with the resulting triple and assesses the Reviewer’s semantic judgment, with the target correspondence and extracted context held fixed across systems.
blocks.zh:
OpenAI数学研究说明了审查主要结果需要解释其正式声明背后的定义和制约因素。
为了使这种审查能够跨系统重复,我们构建了精益审查本克,这是第3.1节所定义的审查实例的可重复使用集合。
每个实例是固定的三相 x = (I t, F t, C) x = (I_{t}, F_{t},\ mathcal{C}) : a 提供的非正式索赔、选定的正式陈述和LeanTrace提取的依赖背景。
MechAlign的Selector和LeanTrace阶段在基准建设中完成.
评价从三重评价开始,评估审查员的语义判断,目标对应和提取的背景在系统之间固定不变。

blocks.en:
As illustrated in Figure 3 (a), the resource contains 501 tasks: the 201 OpenAI Math main-result tasks discussed in Section 4 , 200 targets selected from the Fermat’s Last Theorem (FLT) development, and 100 from the three-dimensional Kakeya development.
For FLT and Kakeya, we select individual theorem declarations throughout the developments, including intermediate results and supporting mathematical infrastructure, and use each selected declaration as the root for a separate LeanTrace extraction.
FLT targets span elementary and algebraic number theory, local ramification, Galois representations, elliptic curves, modular forms, and modularity lifting.
Kakeya targets cover geometric configurations, shading and density, covering and scale estimates, Frostman-type conditions, and intermediate lemmas leading to dimension bounds.
This selection yields multiple review instances from each development, broadening the mathematical and dependency-structure coverage beyond the OpenAI main-result setting.

对于FLT和Kakeya,我们在整个开发过程中选择单个定理声明,包括中间结果和支持数学基础设施,并使用所选的每个声明作为单独取出LeanTrace的根.
FLT目标跨越基本数和代数数理论,局部拉米化,加洛瓦表示法,椭圆曲线,模块化形式,和模块化提升.

这种选择从每个发展动态中产生多个审查实例,将数学和依赖结构的涵盖范围扩大到OpenAI主成果设定之外。

blocks.en:
To construct each instance, we pin the upstream source and interpretation environment, select a root declaration, and prepare a statement project that retains definition and instance values and structure constraints while replacing theorem proofs with placeholders.
LeanTrace extracts the root’s retained dependency graph to form 𝒞 \mathcal{C} .
An explicit declaration mapping associates F t F_{t} with its supplied description and qualifications, which together specify I t I_{t} .
We freeze the triple together with provenance and available annotations; reference labels remain separate from the model input.
FLT descriptions were recovered from Lean-generated documentation, while Kakeya uses upstream comments and explicitly marked model-authored Lean paraphrases, with the source breakdown given in Appendix C .
Compilation records, graph checks, and release validation check artifact integrity without certifying semantic alignment.
Appendix C gives construction, mapping, validation, and detailed statistics.

OpenAI’s internal dependency counts are strongly right-skewed: the median is 17 declarations, and the middle half of tasks spans 7–38, while the largest context contains 1,041 internal declarations. Released reference labels are provisional model judgments; accuracy against human-adjudicated references remains to be established.

blocks.en: 6 Discussion and Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6. 讨论和结论

blocks.en: We present MechAlign for reviewing whether a selected Lean result expresses its supplied informal claim through the project declarations that determine its meaning. LeanTrace extracts and organizes these dependencies, enabling the Reviewer to investigate semantic discrepancies and cite supporting evidence. Our preliminary OpenAI Math review and HyperbolicObstruction case illustrate this process, while LeanReviewBench provides 501 fixed review instances from OpenAI Math, Fermat’s Last Theorem, and Kakeya for reproducible studies of evidence acquisition and semantic judgment.

blocks.en: Limitations and Future Works. The extracted context excludes proof bodies and stops at the external-library boundary, so it may leave essential interpretation evidence unavailable; alignment review also does not certify the original proofs or their axiomatic assumptions. Some informal descriptions are Lean-derived, reference labels remain provisional, and shared developments and possible training exposure limit generalization claims. Future work will validate descriptions against independent mathematical sources, obtain human-adjudicated judgments, and complete controlled comparisons of statement-only, full-project, and dependency-guided reviews to assess judgment quality, evidence localization, and cost.
blocks.zh: 限制和未来工程。 所提取的上下文排除了证明机构,并停留在外部图书馆边界上,因此可能使基本解释证据无法提供;对齐审查也不证明原始证据或其逻辑假设。 一些非正式的描述取自精益,参考标签仍然是暂时的,共享的发展和可能的培训曝光限制了泛化索赔. 今后的工作将对照独立的数学来源验证描述,获得经人判断的判断,并完成对只陈述、全项目和依赖性指导的审查的控制性比较,以评估判断质量、证据本地化和成本。

blocks.en: The inventory contains 201 OpenAI Math main-result targets, 200 targets from anthropics/fermats-last-theorem , and 100 from project-numina/kakeya-3d . The OpenAI targets are those used in Section 4 . For FLT and Kakeya, we select individual theorem declarations across the developments, including intermediate results and supporting infrastructure. Each selected declaration becomes the root of a separate review triple. Other theorem declarations reached during extraction contribute their types as context; their occurrence in a dependency closure does not create additional tasks.

blocks.en: The selection covers eight areas in FLT and seven in Kakeya (Table 1 ). FLT targets range from elementary and algebraic number theory through local ramification, Galois representations, elliptic curves, modular forms, modular-curve geometry, and modularity lifting. Kakeya targets cover geometric configurations, shading and density, covers and scales, Frostman, Katz–Tao, and Sticky estimates, and intermediate lemmas and bootstrap arguments leading to dimension bounds. The counts document the selected coverage, rather than a representative sample of Lean mathematics. OpenAI’s domain labels use a different granularity and should not be pooled with these areas into a single domain count.

LeanTrace extracts each selected statement F t F_{t} and its dependency context 𝒞 \mathcal{C} under the policy in Section 3 , including the external-library boundary.

blocks.en: An explicit declaration mapping associates the selected statement with a description and any scope qualifications, forming the supplied informal claim I t I_{t} . All 501 tasks have nonempty main descriptions. The 200 FLT descriptions were recovered from upstream HTML documentation generated from Lean. Kakeya’s 100 preferred descriptions comprise 82 upstream comments (82%) and 18 explicitly marked model-authored Lean paraphrases (18%). The latter include the description of KakeyaDimensionThree ; the other 17 expand terse comments and retain explicit hypotheses. All six target statements with an explicit StickyFrostman hypothesis preserve it in their preferred descriptions. Original comments and description origins remain in the accompanying informal records.
blocks.zh: 明确的声明绘图将选定的声明与描述和任何范围限制联系起来,构成所提供的非正式索赔It I_{t}。 所有501项任务都有非空地的主要描述. 200份FLT说明是从Lean生成的上游HTML文档中取出. Kakeya的100个首选描述包括82个上游评论(82%)和18个明确标出模型作者的Lean 参数(18%). 后者包括Kakeya Dimension Three的描述;而其他17个扩展了terse的评论并保留了明确的假设. 所有6个目标声明都带有明显的"粘着"(StickyFrostman)假说,将其保留在其首选描述中. 原始评论和说明的出处保留在所附的非正式记录中。

blocks.en: For 32 Kakeya targets, the records also contain checked, page-linked background from the Guth–Wang–Zahl paper, identified as paper_context . Such passages provide background rather than replacing the mapped target description or asserting its equivalence with Lean. For example, Main Lemma 1 in the paper has no exponent loss, whereas the selected Lean result requires β < γ \beta<\gamma . The records distinguish descriptions, qualifications, and paper context through explicit mapping relations; missing auxiliary descriptions remain absent. Agreement with a Lean-derived description supports a supplied-text consistency test, while source-grounded alignment requires a reviewed independent specification.
blocks.zh: 对于32个Kakeya目标,记录中还包含来自Guth–Wang–Zahl文件的已检查的、与页面相链接的背景,这些背景被确定为paper_context. 这种段落提供了背景,而不是取代所绘制的目标描述或申明其与Lean的等同性。 例如,论文中的Main Lemma 1没有引人注意的损失,而所选取的Lean结果则需要β < < β\beta<\gamma。 这些记录通过明确的绘图关系来区分描述、资格和纸张上下文;缺失的辅助描述仍然缺失。 与精益出处描述的协议支持提供文本的一致性测试,而基于源的对齐则需要经过审查的独立规格.

blocks.en: The resulting triples are frozen in tasks.jsonl , accompanied by Lean text artifacts and provenance-rich informal records. Evaluation inputs are exported from these frozen packages without reparsing the Lean files or rebuilding the extraction environment. Formal declarations and dependency edges determine the retained context. Description origins, review status, preparation metadata, and reference labels are kept outside the exported model input.
blocks.zh: 由此产生的三重奏被冻结在"任务". jsonl",并配有精益文字文物和出处丰富的非正式记录. 从这些被冻结的软件包中输出评价投入,而不重新分解Lean文件或重建取出环境。 正式申报和依赖关系决定保留上下文。 描述出处、审查状况、准备元数据、参考标签都保存在输出模型输入之外。

blocks.en: C.3 Context Statistics and Release Validation
blocks.zh: C.3 背景统计和发布验证

blocks.en: Figure 3 (b) reports the distribution of per-task internal dependency counts, combining the selected definition/structure inventory and remaining internal declarations. Counts exclude main statements and external-library boundary nodes; boxes show the first and third quartiles and median, and whiskers show the full observed range.
blocks.zh: 图3(b)报告了每个任务内部依赖性计数的分布情况,将选定的定义/结构清单和其余内部申报合并在一起。 计数排除了主语句和外部-图书馆边界节点;框中显示第一和第三克和中位数,而胡须显示观测到的全部范围.

blocks.en: In FLT, 64 of the 200 tasks (32%) have no internal dependency declarations beyond the root. Each nevertheless retains between 4 and 130 external-library boundary nodes. Such roots are expressed through library declarations whose identities and types are retained without recursive expansion. A zero internal count therefore does not imply an empty context; a boundary type may still be insufficient if a judgment requires the library implementation.
blocks.zh: 在FLT中,200项任务中有64项(32%)除根外没有内部依赖性申报。 然而,每个都保留了4至130个外部图书馆边界节点。 这种根源通过图书馆声明来表达,这些声明的特性和类型不重复地予以保留。 因此,零内部计数并不意味着空上下文;如果判决要求执行库,边界类型可能仍然不足。

blocks.en: The frozen packages separately enumerate a selected definition/structure inventory in their definitions field. Summing these entries across tasks gives 3,477 for OpenAI, 1,155 for FLT, and 1,191 for Kakeya, for a total of 5,823 occurrences. These entries are only part of the retained context, not a count of all internal declarations or of unique definitions. Shared declarations can occur in multiple tasks, and all three collections include tasks with no entries in this field. Table 2 additionally reports retained internal declarations by kind, including definitions, structures, abbreviations, constructors, classes, and supporting theorem types. These statistics characterize context size and composition rather than established semantic difficulty.
blocks.zh: 被冻结的软件包在其定义领域单独列出一个选定的定义/结构清单。 对这些条目进行跨任务组合后,OpenAI可得到3,477个条目,FLT可得到1,155个条目,Kakeya可得到1,191个条目,共计5,823个条目。 这些条目只是保留上下文的一部分,而不是所有内部声明或独特定义的一数. 共享声明可以在多个任务中发生,而所有三个集合都包含这个领域没有条目的任务. 表2还按种类保留了内部申报,包括定义、结构、缩略语、构建器、类别和辅助定理类型。 这些统计数据是背景大小和构成的特点,而不是既定的语义困难。

blocks.en: Compilation checks statement types and retained definition bodies in the pinned environment; theorem proofs remain placeholders. Archived closure replay checks the extraction record, while the release validator checks file hashes, target inventories, description mappings, graph consistency, and reference/input bindings. These checks establish artifact integrity without certifying proof correctness or semantic alignment.
blocks.zh: 编译检查说明书类型和所保留的定义机构在被绑定的环境中;定理证明仍然是占位符. 已归档的关闭重放检查提取记录,而发布验证器检查文件散列,目标目录,描述映射,图表一致性,以及参考/输入绑定. 这些检查确定了文物的完整性,但没有证明证据正确或语义一致。

blocks.en: The release includes provisional model judgments for all 501 tasks; descriptions and semantic references remain pending human adjudication. Repeated evaluations should record task and model identities, execution configuration, budgets, and execution outcomes, retaining collection and provenance breakdowns. Any held-out split must also account for shared source developments and overlapping dependencies.
blocks.zh: 释放内容包括所有501项任务的临时示范判决;描述和语义参考仍然有待人类裁决。 重复进行的评价应记录任务和模式身份、执行配置、预算和执行结果,保留收集和来源细目。 任何搁置的分裂还必须考虑到共同来源的发展和重叠的依赖性。

blocks.en: C.4 Code and Data Availability
blocks.zh: C.4 代码和数据可用性

blocks.en:
The MechAlign implementation, including the LeanTrace extraction tool, and the LeanReviewBench data and evaluation tools will be made publicly available upon publication at https://github.com/MechMath/MechAlign and https://github.com/MechMath/PaperLeanBench , respectively.
The benchmark repository provides the frozen review instances, provenance records, provisional reference labels, and evaluation tools described above.
blocks.zh:
MechAlign的执行,包括LeanTrace提取工具,以及LeanReview Bench的数据和评价工具,将在https://github.com/MechMath/MechAlign和https://github.com/MechMath/PaperLean Bench上公布。
基准储存库提供上述被冻结的审查实例、出处记录、临时参考标签和评价工具。

blocks.en:
The released system supports explicitly supplied claim–declaration mappings, fresh dependency extraction, and six-dimension review with quotation checks.
The original-paper locator is limited to pinned OpenAI TeX sources and archived target mappings; general manuscript search and automatic target selection are not implemented by the release.
Benchmark evaluation uses the frozen supplied claim and dependency context without repeating selection or extraction; the MechAlign adapter assesses the main claim and encodes undetermined as insufficient_information in protocol submissions.
blocks.zh:
释放的系统支持明确提供的索赔-声明绘图、新的依赖性提取和带有报价核对的六分法审查。
原始纸质定位器仅限于被绑定的OpenAI TeX源和存档目标映射;一般手稿搜索和自动目标选择没有被发布所执行.
基准评价使用冻结提供的债权和依赖性上下文,而不重复选择或提取;MechAlign适配器评估主要债权,并将未确定的编码为协议提交材料中的不充分_信息.
